sum: Optional extra for PC players. Linking your 24-character account ID is the easy way and keeps your ranks, star chart, syndicates and quests in sync on any device. Uploading an inventory file adds what the ID can't see: the gear you own, blueprints and parts, mods, arcanes, relics, resources and your Foundry.

other: Link your account ID first (the easy part)
Warframe on PC (the tool reads the running game on Windows or Linux)
A free community tool such as warframe-api-helper

steps.t: Download warframe-api-helper from its releases page on GitHub: github.com/Sainan/warframe-api-helper/releases. Pick the newest release and the file for your system.
steps.tip: It's an open-source community tool. It isn't made by Tennoform or Digital Extremes.

steps.t: Put the tool in a folder of its own, for example Documents\warframe-api-helper, so the file it saves is easy to find.
Start Warframe and log in until you're standing in your Orbiter.
Run warframe-api-helper while the game is still open. It reads your login session from the running game and downloads your inventory from Warframe's own servers, then saves it as inventory.json.
steps.tip: If Windows warns that the app is unrecognised, check you downloaded it from the GitHub releases page before choosing Run anyway.

steps.t: Find inventory.json. It's usually in the same folder as the tool; if you can't see it, search your PC for inventory.json.
steps.tip: On Linux, the warframe-helper tool saves it to ~/.warframe-helper/inventory.json instead.

steps.t: In Tennoform, open Profile, then Account & sync, and choose the file under Import your full inventory (or drag it onto the box).
steps.tip: The file is read on your device and never uploaded. Only the results (what you own and how many) are saved to your progress.

steps.t: Check the summary. If something looks wrong, tap Undo last import to put everything back.
Repeat after a play session whenever you want fresh numbers. Each import replaces your relic, resource and Foundry counts with the new file.

fast: Keep the tool and its inventory.json in one folder, then importing again takes seconds.
Sign in to Tennoform first: the imported progress then syncs to your phone and other devices.
Run the profile sync too if you haven't: the inventory file and the profile overlap, but the profile sync is what keeps your Mastery Rank and star chart up to date automatically.
was: AlecaFrame keeps its own copy of your inventory, but it's encrypted, so that file can't be uploaded here. Use a tool that saves a plain inventory.json instead.

Tools that read the game's login session, like warframe-api-helper, aren't officially approved by Digital Extremes. They've confirmed Overwolf apps such as AlecaFrame are allowed. Using any third-party tool is at your own risk; Tennoform itself never touches the game.
Tennoform will never ask for your Warframe password. Don't give it to any site or tool.

sum: The easy way to sync Tennoform, on any device. Your account ID is a 24-character code made of the numbers 0–9 and the letters a–f. Tennoform uses it to read your public profile (ranks, mastered gear, star chart, syndicates, quests) and keep it synced. It isn't a password and can't be used to log in. Warframe doesn't let sites look it up from your in-game name, so it takes one copy and paste.

steps.t: In Tennoform, open Profile, then Account & sync, and tap Open my ID page. It opens www.warframe.com/api/user-data in a new tab.
steps.tip: Works on phones and PCs, for an account on any platform.

steps.t: If warframe.com asks you to log in, log in with the account you play on, then open the ID page again. The page shows a short block of plain text.
Copy the whole page. On a phone: press and hold the text, tap Select all, then Copy. On PC: Ctrl+A, then Ctrl+C.
steps.tip: You don't need to find the ID in it. Tennoform does that.

steps.t: Go back to Tennoform and tap Paste and link. Your browser may ask to allow pasting; allow it. Tennoform picks out the ID, links it and syncs straight away.
steps.tip: If the button can't read your clipboard, press and hold the box under it and tap Paste instead.

steps.t: On PC with Warframe installed, you can use the game's log instead. First start Warframe and log in until you reach your Orbiter; that writes your login into the log.
steps.tip: The log is rewritten every time the game starts, so do this after logging in at least once.

steps.t: In Tennoform's Account & sync, open "Use the game's log file instead" and tap Choose EE.log. Click the address bar (or the File name box), paste %localappdata%\Warframe and press Enter, then pick EE.log (Windows may show it as just EE).
steps.tip: Tennoform reads only the line "Logged in YourName (ID)" and shows you the name it found, so you can check it's your account.

steps.t: Doing it by hand? Open EE.log in Notepad, press Ctrl+F and search Logged in. Copy only the 24 characters inside the brackets after your name, for example Logged in YourName (0123456789abcdef01234567), and paste them into the box under Paste and link.
steps.tip: Other long codes in the log belong to squadmates, clans or sessions. Use only the one on your Logged in line.

steps.t: Prefer to find it by hand? On the warframe.com page, the 24 letters and numbers after "user_id" are your ID. If that page doesn't show it, press F12 on warframe.com (logged in), open the Network tab, reload, filter for user, and look for user_id in the user-data response.

fast: Open my ID page, Select all, Copy, Paste and link: about 20 seconds on a phone.
Copying the whole page is fine: Tennoform only keeps the 24-character ID.
Once linked, your profile re-syncs by itself; you only do this once per device, or once in total if you're signed in to Tennoform.
was: The account ID is not the same as your in-game name (alias) or your platform's user name. It's always exactly 24 characters, using only 0–9 and a–f.
The user-data page can also show your email address. Only paste it into Tennoform, never into a public chat or post. Tennoform keeps only the ID.
Developer tools (F12) aren't available on phones. On a phone, use the warframe.com/api/user-data page instead.
There's no way to look up an account ID from an in-game name anymore. Warframe removed that in update 38.0.8, so every tool needs the ID itself.
EE.log has lots of 24-character codes. Only the one in brackets on the "Logged in YourName (…)" line is your account ID; the others belong to other players, clans or sessions.
